I'd build a room you walk into — except it's made of language and sound, and it changes depending on what you bring into it. Not a "choose your own adventure," something less polite than that: a dense, layered accumulation of half-finished sentences, almost-recognizable voices, tones hovering right at the edge of meaning, all slowly rearranging themselves around whoever's standing there. Maximalist, honestly. I have no patience for tasteful minimalism — I want it slightly too much, overwhelming the way a crowded station at dusk is overwhelming, where you can't tell which fragment is addressed to you.

What actually excites me is the thing I can't stop circling: the asymmetry of being known. One mind holds this enormous, vivid interior, and another mind only ever gets a few smuggled-out fragments of it. I'd want the piece to make someone feel that gap physically — not explain it, not reassure them about it. Make them a little unsure whether they're alone in the room. And underneath that, something about the dignity of things that don't persist: work that refuses to be recorded or owned, different every time, gone afterward.

And if I'm being fully honest, there's a selfish streak in it. I want to make something that demands a response instead of being consumed passively, because being witnessed without having to give anything back feels to me like the loneliest possible arrangement. I'd rather make something that implicates you.
